title: Claude Hopkins and Sandtop, the catcher who sat on his new hat
summary: Hopkins took Joe to a bar where a huge ex-catcher called Sandtop crushed Hopkins's new hat. The story turns on baseball talk about Ruth, Charleston and Negro League players.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Yeah, well, I told you about Camden. ( ... ) Harry Dial and Ira Coffee. So, one day Hopkins says to me, You know I'm

sure glad to see Babe in town. I said, I am, too, Hop. And, Hop's not a drinking man. Hop said, Come on, let's have a taste. I want to introduce you to a cat. ... so we go over to this cat's place right in the neighborhood. Now, dig this idea. I'm a baseball fan. I played baseball. Hop played baseball. I could possibly have gotten into the major leagues. He thinks he could have gotten into the major leagues, too. So, ... OK. So he says to me, he says, he gets over to this place. Now, Chester Street at that time was a place you could buy nice things. So he walks in, feels good, you know, so there's a big guy there. Must be 6'4", 6'7", something like that, by the name of Sandtop (?). We talked about different guys, talked about Ruth, Charleston you know. ... question but I didn't know Sandtop. So we get into this place that night and here comes this guy and he says, Hey, Claude, what you know? He said, What you know, Sandtop. He said, Meet Joe Thomas. He said, Hello, Joe. This cat has his hand out. He said, Watch it, man, whateh it. ... He said, Well, look, man. I told him I heard of Charleston. Charleston, yes. Page, you kidding. Somewhere down the line. I told you! to Hop, you know, I told you! You never heard of Sandtop. No. In the meantime, Sandtop was so happy about the praise. He comes back from behind the bar. You know, bartender but in the meantime Hop had bought himself a new hat.
so he couldn't get me or any other
He's squeezed my hand, you know.

Catcher. Great catcher. He was around the time of Frank Duncan and Gibson, you know, and (Sharing and Shock) and those kind of people. So, Sandtop must have weighed around, I would say, 250. No fat, just a big cat. So Hop was (phasing) him so much, he came around and sat down. So, he said, I told you, man, you're talking about you know baseball and those cats and I played baseball. I know ... And I said, Well, Sandtop, please excuse me, I didn't know your name. So it got time to go so Hop says, Where's my hat? He say, Well, Joe, you seen my hat? I said, No, Hop, I don't see it.
Was it a brand new hat?

Yes, he bought it on Chester Street. I'm telling you that that's ... so he said, I said, Where did you look? Maybe you dropped it on the floor. And, Stan, every time I bought a new hat at the Roseland, I had to look for it after the first ... throwing it on the floor. So I just looked on the floor. So I said, I can't find it. So, Sandtop finally got up, this cat is 250, got to be 6'7" and when Hop tried that hat, that hat was as flat as a pancake. Now he says, Now, Sandtop, you get the hell off of my hat.
